eventVenue: Blockchain Innovation Hub, ZamZam Complex, New Garage, Ibadan, Nigeria
eventDescription: CrossFi Dev. Series 3.0 in Ibadan brought together developers, founders, and enthusiasts for a full day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, and demos of open-source builder tools on CrossFi. The series highlighted real-world use cases, ecosystem grants, and how African teams can ship on CrossFi Chain.

eventName: Exploring the Future of Financial Connectivity on CrossFi Chain
eventDescription: A deep-dive campus session on financial connectivity through CrossFi Chain — bridging traditional finance and on-chain systems, payment flows, and the role of blockchain in borderless, programmable money for emerging markets.

A comparative university workshop on DeFi versus TradFi — risks, regulation, user experience, and where both worlds converge. Students discussed stablecoins, remittances, compliance, and how builders can design products that serve real African users.

eventVenue: Federal University of Technology Akure (FUTA), Akure, Ogun State, Nigeria
eventDescription: CrossFi Africa and DLT Africa hosted a university session at FUTA on the future of decentralized finance — onboarding both developers and non-developers into the CrossFi ecosystem. Attendees explored DeFi fundamentals, CrossFi Chain tooling, and how on-chain finance can expand access for students and young builders in Nigeria.

eventName: Unlocking the Potential of CrossFi Chain
eventDescription: An introductory university talk on CrossFi Chain — architecture, use cases, and why interoperable payment infrastructure matters for Africa. Attendees explored wallets, cross-chain concepts, and real-world scenarios where CrossFi tooling applies.

eventVenue: DLT Africa Tech Hub, Ota, Ogun State, Nigeria
eventDescription: The CrossFi Mainnet Launch Party at DLT Africa Tech Hub celebrated the official debut of CrossFi’s mainnet — an evening of networking, demos, and community energy. Builders, partners, and enthusiasts gathered to mark a major milestone for CrossFi in Africa with food, conversations, and launch-day announcements.

DLT Africa partnered with Lisk Africa for BlockChange — a continent-wide virtual hackathon on the Lisk platform. Builders across Africa turned blockchain ideas into working prototypes, with mentorship, technical resources, and a path from concept to deployable solutions on Lisk.

A recap of Lisk Africa’s April university outreach — campus sessions, student onboarding, and community activations that introduced the next generation of developers to building on Lisk. Highlights from multiple institutions and grassroots Web3 adoption across the region.

Code Quest 2.0 brought Kenyan developers into a hands-on Lisk workshop covering smart contracts, dApp fundamentals, and practical build workflows. Participants left with clearer paths to ship on Lisk and join the wider Lisk Africa builder community.

An online Lisk Launchpad session for founders and developers exploring how to validate ideas, structure MVPs, and launch on the Lisk ecosystem. The workshop covered tooling, grants context, and go-to-market basics for early-stage Web3 projects in Africa.

eventVenue: DLT Africa Tech Hub, Ota, Ogun State, Nigeria
eventDescription: Celo Africa DAO ran a hands-on workshop at the DLT Africa hub — covering Celo contracts, local stablecoins, and building for real users on mobile. Participants practiced deploying and testing small apps in a collaborative, mentor-led environment.

eventVenue: DLT Africa Tech Hub, Ota, Ogun State, Nigeria
eventDescription: The closing day of Celo Nigeria Code Jam — teams finalized submissions, demoed projects, and received feedback from mentors and judges. Winners and standout builders were celebrated as part of DLT Africa’s ongoing partnership with the Celo ecosystem.

eventVenue: DLT Africa Tech Hub, Ota, Ogun State, Nigeria
eventDescription: The Celo Nigeria Code Jam at DLT Africa brought developers together for an intensive build day on Celo — mobile-first dApps, stable assets, and miniPay-style experiences. Teams prototyped, pitched, and connected with the Celo Africa DAO community.
